threats.protected: Inner Controller confidentiality, integrity, endpoint authentication, capability and revocation checks remain G20.1 end-to-end properties.
threats.not_protected: The operator observes source IP, route occupancy, connection timing, direction and ciphertext size.
threats.mitigation: Forward sealed Controller frames unchanged; never terminate inner authentication at the relay.
threats.residual_metadata: IP address, route ID, timing, direction and size.

threats.protected: A client without the relay-scoped signing credential cannot occupy a route.
threats.not_protected: Public endpoint existence and aggregate rejection timing remain visible.
threats.mitigation: Single-use bounded challenge, Ed25519 proof, route and role binding, connection limits.
threats.residual_metadata: Source IP and aggregate rejection code.

threats.protected: A stolen device route credential cannot authenticate as Host or decrypt Controller ciphertext.
threats.not_protected: It can occupy that device route until revocation and cause denial of service.
threats.mitigation: Separate Host/device credentials, role-bound proof, revocation epoch and replacement procedure.
threats.residual_metadata: Affected route occupancy and revocation event.

threats.protected: Modified inner frames fail Controller-v1 AEAD authentication.
threats.not_protected: An attacker can drop, duplicate or delay opaque frames.
threats.mitigation: Inner sequence/authentication plus explicit reconnect; no mutation acknowledgement at relay.

threats.protected: Admission proof replay and envelope version mismatch fail closed; inner protocol version and sequence remain authenticated.
threats.mitigation: Consume every challenge once, bind epoch/version/role/route, exact monotonic direction sequence.

threats.protected: Aggregate bounded security events can establish limit/revocation actions without content logs.
threats.not_protected: Ciphertext-only logs cannot prove the plaintext command or user intent.
threats.mitigation: Do not claim content auditability; retain only approved aggregate operational evidence.
threats.residual_metadata: Aggregate counts and coarse time buckets if later approved.

threats.protected: TLS can protect relay admission and outer transport; inner Controller crypto protects content from the relay.
threats.not_protected: IP address, timing, volume and ciphertext length are not hidden; TLS is not anonymity.
threats.mitigation: Explicit disclosure, no anonymity claim, optional direct routes, consider coarse padding only in a separately reviewed goal.
threats.residual_metadata: IP address, timing, size and provider region.

threats.protected: Default spike stats contain aggregate counts only.
threats.not_protected: Infrastructure access logs may contain IP and timing under provider policy.
threats.mitigation: No route IDs, credentials, payloads, per-frame sizes or per-route timing in application logs; define retention before operation.

threats.protected: Frame, per-route queue, 64 MiB global queue, route and challenge bounds prevent unbounded in-process allocation.
threats.not_protected: Authorized traffic can consume the configured quota and bandwidth.
threats.mitigation: Per-route and global quotas, global admission limits, backpressure close, external rate/DDoS controls for any public operation.

threats.protected: Two-MiB/32-frame directional queue caps stop unbounded buffering.
threats.not_protected: The route can be disconnected and lose in-flight ciphertext.
threats.mitigation: Return backpressure, close exact route, clear memory and require end-to-end resynchronization.

threats.protected: Only one Host and one Controller occupy a route; opaque 256-bit IDs resist guessing.
threats.not_protected: A stolen credential can still race the legitimate endpoint.
threats.mitigation: Duplicate fail-closed, rate limits, revocation and no user-derived route identifiers.

threats.protected: Relay admission grants forwarding only and cannot grant inner Controller capabilities.
threats.not_protected: A legitimately paired Controller retains its persisted G20 capabilities until revoked.
threats.mitigation: Keep relay credentials separate from G20 keys and recheck inner capability/revocation at Host.

threats.protected: No ciphertext is persisted or replayed; only public admission metadata may be reconstructed.
threats.not_protected: All active routes disconnect and in-flight output is lost.
threats.mitigation: Clients reconnect explicitly and use Host replay semantics; never report relay mutation success.

threats.protected: Connection-local challenge ticks avoid wall-clock dependence in the prototype.
threats.not_protected: Production multi-instance expiry needs a bounded monotonic/server-time design.
threats.mitigation: Keep challenge lifetime short, single-use and instance-local; fail closed after restart.

threats.adversary: compromised image, TLS key or deployment secret
threats.protected: Inner Controller crypto still prevents a relay-only compromise from reading or forging content.
threats.not_protected: A compromised binary can deny service, collect metadata, weaken admission or serve a malicious update.
threats.mitigation: Pinned Rust dependencies, cargo-deny, signed OCI/release artifacts, least privilege, key rotation and incident runbook before beta.
threats.residual_metadata: All metadata visible to the compromised deployment.

threats.protected: Relay has no plaintext or offline content store to disclose.
threats.not_protected: Operator/provider may hold IP, account, payment, timing and infrastructure logs.
threats.mitigation: No operated service under D05; approve regions/processors/retention/subpoena process and privacy terms first.
threats.residual_metadata: Provider account, IP, timing, region and aggregate usage.
